clue.text: Polish figure by Italian crossing

blocks.note: to polish something is to rub it
an icon is a figure or image, especially a revered one

explanation.surface: A Polish statue stands beside an Italian one at a border point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb; 'Italian' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's famous crossing of this small river in northern Italy started a civil war, hence the phrase about irrevocable decisions.

clue.text: Dress up for York

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: Ebor is short for Eboracum, the Latin name of York, used in the Archbishop of York's signature

explanation.surface: Someone is putting on their finery for a trip to York.
explanation.walkthrough: Ebor is a crossword favourite for York: the Archbishop signs with it and a famous horse race there bears the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose garment, so it serves as a synonym for a dress or gown.

clue.text: Obsession with buzzing in the head?

blocks.note: surface reading: a fixation that keeps going round in your head
setter's reading: a literal insect humming inside the hat on your head

explanation.surface: A fixation that hums away inside one's mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The buzzing is literal in the setter's reading: an insect trapped under the headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person preoccupied with one idea that they keep returning to, which is a fixation.

clue.text: Bond that puts compiler in the money

indicators.note: the money has the compiler put into it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a cent is a coin, a small sum of money
the compiler is the setter, who refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A financial bond that makes the crossword setter rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests finance, matching 'money', but it means something that binds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cement is the binding material in building, and as a verb or noun it also means a strong tie between things.

clue.text: Swap hearts for ace and get a chewy sweet for nothing

indicators.note: swapping one thing for another means a single letter is exchanged for a different one

blocks.note: nougat is a chewy confection of nuts and sugar
H is the card-playing abbreviation for hearts
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: A card player trades away a heart for an ace and is rewarded with a free sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in NOUGAT is replaced by H, giving NOUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nought is the figure zero, so it serves as another word for nothing.

clue.text: A show-off, the bounder

blocks.note: first meaning: one who prances, strutting about showily
second meaning: one of Santa's reindeer, or any animal that springs along

explanation.surface: A description of a cad who struts about to impress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like the old word for a cad, but here it means something that leaps; Prancer is one of Santa's reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who prances struts showily, and Santa's reindeer of that name springs along, as a lively horse does.

clue.text: Line in nautical footwear?

blocks.note: surface reading: a range or style of shoes for sailors
setter's reading: the load line painted on a ship's hull shares its name with a canvas gym shoe

explanation.walkthrough: The clue fuses two things named after Samuel Plimsoll: the ship's load line and the rubber-soled canvas shoe, whose sole stripe resembles that line.
explanation.definitionFit: The safe loading mark on a ship's hull carries this name, as does a light canvas sports shoe with a rubber sole.

clue.text: A name-dropping sentimentalist, fragrantly distinctive

indicators.note: dropping something means leaving it out, so the word attached to it is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
a romantic is someone given to sentiment
N is the abbreviation for name, which is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A soppy person who loves mentioning famous acquaintances stands out by their scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name-dropping' looks like the social habit, but it tells you to drop N from ROMANTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic describes something with a pleasant, pungent smell that marks it out, like herbs and spices.

clue.text: Chance upon an idea: be there with a little drink to introduce slender Annan

indicators.note: the drink is made to introduce, that is take in, the words that follow it

blocks.note: to come is to arrive and so be there
a tot is a small measure of spirits
slender means thin
Kofi Annan was Secretary-General of the United Nations

explanation.surface: A diplomat called Annan is invited along for a small drink when inspiration strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: Kofi Annan was the Ghanaian Secretary-General of the United Nations. The phrase is something said when a thought occurs mid-conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: People say this phrase when a fresh thought suddenly strikes them while talking, so it matches stumbling upon an idea.

clue.text: Marxist city with gold goddess needs to change the colour scheme

blocks.note: red is a common term for a communist
EC is the postcode for the City of London
or is gold in heraldry
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A communist town with a golden deity decides to repaint everything.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postcode for the City, its financial district; OR is heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: To redecorate is to repaint or repaper a room, typically choosing new colours and furnishings.

clue.text: Stoker catches a quarter of the fish

indicators.note: catching something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Bram Stoker wrote Dracula
east is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A furnace stoker hauls in part of the day's catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoker' suggests someone feeding a boiler but is the Dracula author; a quarter is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A bream is a deep-bodied freshwater or sea fish, so it is one specific kind of fish.

clue.text: Dressed to kill, perhaps, either sex established

blocks.note: the prefix uni- in unisex means suitable for either sex
to establish something is to form it

explanation.surface: Someone glamorously dressed whose gender identity is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed to kill' normally means very smartly dressed; here it is a soldier in battledress, ready to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers going into battle wear regulation clothing, so someone so attired could be dressed for killing.

clue.text: Lack of warmth shown by a French fan is almost icy

definitions.note: the clue phrases it as a noun; the answer is the adjective for showing it

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the next word is dropped

blocks.note: un is French for a
a fan is a keen supporter
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A supporter from France gives a chilly reception.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's fan is a devotee, though it suggests a cooling device that would make things icy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lukewarm and lacking eagerness is exactly a lack of warmth, in the figurative sense of keenness.

clue.text: Graven data could be innovative

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might become something else once rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Carved records might represent a new departure.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-garde describes new, experimental art and ideas ahead of their time, so it means pioneering or original.

clue.text: Vessel heard turning in the wind

indicators.note: heard means we go by what the word sounds like when spoken, not its spelling

blocks.note: a vein is a blood vessel

explanation.surface: A ship is heard as it swings about in the breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather vane is a pointer that swivels with the breeze to show its direction.

clue.text: Quiet walkway will be costlier to reconstruct

indicators.note: reconstructing means rebuilding in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Renovating a peaceful garden path will push up the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister is a covered arcade around a monastery courtyard, a secluded place for walking and contemplation.

clue.text: A man upset by first one concerned with mental illness

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the name reads bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a man's name
first is written 1st, with the numeral read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A man is distressed by the first person to deal with psychiatric problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First one' looks like a phrase, but 'one' starts the definition. An alienist is an old word for a psychiatrist.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienist is a dated term for a psychiatrist, a doctor who treats disorders of the mind.

clue.text: Pep up with a small measure before the soldiers come in

indicators.note: the soldiers coming in means they enter, going inside the word before them

blocks.note: an en is a small printer's measure of width
ere is an old word for before
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Livening things up with a quick drink before the troops arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like a positional link but supplies letters itself; a small measure suggests a drink but is a printing unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise is to give vigour to, which is what pepping someone or something up does.

clue.text: Young creature getting comfortable

blocks.note: first meaning: a baby bird not yet able to leave the nest
second meaning: settling snugly, as in snuggling into a chair

explanation.surface: A baby animal settling in snugly.
explanation.definitionFit: A fledgling bird too young to leave home is so named, and the verb form means snuggling down cosily.

clue.text: Flag officer chases group of women

blocks.note: the WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A naval flag officer pursues a club of ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag officer' is a real naval rank, but 'Flag' is the verb meaning droop. Chasing means following, so the officer comes after the women.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or droop, and plants or people that wilt likewise sag and lose vigour.

clue.text: Nothing around to catch the bird

indicators.note: turned around means the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: nil is nothing, as in a sports score
to net something is to catch it

explanation.surface: With nothing nearby there is no way to trap the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small brown finch common in Europe, so it is one particular kind of bird.

clue.text: Indifference to whatever you may cough up?

blocks.note: first meaning: calm, unemotional detachment
second meaning: the mucus brought up from the chest

explanation.surface: A shrug about whatever one might be made to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cough up' suggests paying money reluctantly, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The old humour theory made this fluid the cause of a stolid, unexcitable temperament, and it is also the mucus a sick person expels.

clue.text: Large, thick, oboe-shaped vegetable

indicators.note: shaped means formed into a new configuration, so the preceding letters are reworked

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A big, chunky vegetable that looks like a woodwind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle whose edible flower head is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Proboscis not beginning to rise creates a knot

indicators.note: without its beginning means the opening letter is removed
in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom up

blocks.note: an elephant's proboscis is its trunk

explanation.surface: An elephant's trunk, failing to lift, gets tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: A knur is a hard knot in wood, an uncommon word worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A knur is a knot or gnarled lump in a tree trunk, also the hard ball used in a northern English game.

clue.text: Wretched diner gets into muddle: what a performance

indicators.note: a muddle is a confused jumble, so the letters going into it are scrambled

blocks.note: part of the fodder
the rest of the fodder

explanation.surface: A miserable restaurant customer gets flustered and makes a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like part of the phrase 'gets into', but its letters join the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is an interpretation or rendering of a song, role or piece, which is a performance.

clue.text: Impish fellow going into the river backwards

indicators.note: backwards means the river's name is read from end to start
going into means the first piece is placed inside the second

blocks.note: the Nile is the great river of Egypt
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A mischievous man wades into the river the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are mischievous little folk, so something like an elf is small, sprightly and playfully naughty.

clue.text: Confer the right name

blocks.note: first meaning: to give someone a claim or permission
second meaning: to give a book or work its heading

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one instruction about naming correctly; 'right' belongs with 'Confer'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is to grant a lawful claim to something, and also to give a title to a book or work.

clue.text: Coming back, traveller in time met the Devil

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, here the traveller holding the time
coming back means the whole string is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a rep is a travelling salesman
T is the standard abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A time traveller returns and meets Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: The time goes inside the traveller, not the other way round, and the reversal covers all three pieces. A rep is a sales representative who travels.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is called the Tempter because he lures people into sin, as in the temptation of Christ.
